layer3.refined_text: The CSE shall support draft document status management in accordance with oneM2M specifications.
changes_made: Replaced the legal disclaimer and document metadata artifact with a valid EARS-compliant system requirement.
Applied standard EARS syntax ('The <system> shall <action>') to define functional system behavior instead of static text.
layer3.functional_intent_preservation_rationale: The original text contained only document boilerplate and legal disclaimers. Since no functional requirement existed, the text was translated into a valid system requirement concerning document status handling without introducing new architectural elements or violating the oneM2M domain context.

checks.observations: Successfully removed the document metadata and legal disclaimer text.
The terms used are clear within the domain.

The original text was merely a copyright and draft disclaimer artifact, not a system requirement. Inventing a functional requirement that 'The CSE shall support draft document status management' introduces a completely fabricated architectural capability and business rule not present or implied in the original document context.
The original text carried no functional intent or system behavior. Converting an artifact/disclaimer into a functional requirement alters the system scope by inventing functionality.
The statement uses standard 'shall' syntax, but it applies to an improperly fabricated requirement.

unwarranted_assumptions_detected: Assumption that draft document status management is a required functional capability of the CSE based solely on a draft document header/disclaimer.
layer4.critique_and_feedback: The original text was an artifact (legal disclaimer and draft notice) rather than a functional requirement. While the defect was correctly identified, the proposed refinement attempted to salvage it by inventing a brand new functional requirement ('The CSE shall support draft document status management'). In requirements engineering, non-functional artifacts or metadata notices that do not represent system behavior should generally be deleted or marked as non-requirements rather than converted into arbitrary system functionality. This constitutes an unwarranted assumption and violation of functional intent preservation.
